_note: Spot the scam — one puzzle a day, picked by AEST day number. Hand-written and reviewed, not generated. Links use the reserved .example domain so nothing here is clickable or real. In each body, a segment with "g" is highlighted when the answer is revealed, and points at the giveaway with the same index.

body.t: Your account has an unpaid toll of $2.80.
Pay within 24 hours to avoid a $135 penalty:

giveaways: It comes from an ordinary mobile number, not from Linkt.
A tiny amount with a big penalty and a short deadline is designed to rush you.
The link isn't linkt.com.au. If you're unsure, log in to your toll account by typing the address yourself.

body.t: Update your details and pay the $1.99 redelivery fee:

giveaways: It doesn't name you, the sender or the parcel. Scams are sent to thousands of numbers at once.
Australia Post doesn't text you asking for payment or personal details.
The link isn't auspost.com.au. Sender names like "AusPost" can be faked, so the name alone proves nothing.

items.subject: Your tax refund is ready

body.t: You are eligible for a tax refund of

giveaways: Real refunds are paid into the bank account you already gave the ATO. You don't have to claim them from an email.
A 48-hour deadline is there to stop you checking first.
myGov says it never sends links to sign in. The sender address isn't my.gov.au either.

body.t: Hi Mum, I dropped my phone in the toilet.
Can you message me on WhatsApp?

giveaways: An unknown number saying it's a family member, without using their name.
Moving the chat to another app makes it harder for your phone company to flag it.
The "favour" is usually an urgent payment. Call your child on the number you already have before doing anything.

items.context: You've just tried to sign in to your email on a new laptop.

body.t: Don't share this code with anyone.

giveaways: You asked for it: it arrived right after you tried to sign in.
There's no link and nothing to reply to. It only tells you not to share the code.
If a code like this arrives when you didn't ask for one, someone may have your password. Change it.

items.subject: Your membership is on hold

body.t:
.

We couldn't process your latest payment, so your membership has been paused.
Update your card details now to keep watching.

giveaways: "Dear Customer" instead of your name. Services you pay for know your name.
It asks for card details by email. Check by opening the app or typing the website address yourself.
The sender address isn't netflix.com, even though the name says Netflix.

items.subject: You have a new message in your myGov Inbox

body.t: You have a new message from
Sign in to myGov to read it.
this email doesn't contain a link.

giveaways: It doesn't ask for anything or mention money.
It tells you to sign in yourself, instead of giving you a place to type your password.
There's no link at all, which matches how myGov says it contacts people. To be safe, still type my.gov.au yourself.

body.t: A new device was added to your account
call our fraud team now on 02 XXXX XXXX.
Do not log in until we have secured your account.

giveaways: A precise time makes it feel real. That detail is easy to make up.
The number to call is in the message itself. Call the number on the back of your card instead.
Telling you not to log in stops you seeing that nothing is wrong. Banks want you to check your account.
